thread.title: Dow Gains 19 Points Because a New Year Starts With a Clean Slate

title: Dow Gains 19 Points Because a New Year Starts With a Clean Slate
text:
Dow Gains 19 Points Because a New Year Starts With a Clean Slate By Jan. 2, 2019 5:13 p.m. ET Order Reprints Michael Haddad Text size
Resolute . Futures looked glum this morning, but investors cheered up as the day wore on . The recovery came despite plenty of uncertainty, including a slowing China and a continued government shutdown in the U.S. Luckily, optimism isn’t as limited as January sunshine, and stocks maintained that rally through the close. In today’s After the Bell , we... ...survey the markets' worries; ...and why investors may have ignored them; and ...watch Arconic shine. New Year, Who ‘Dis?
Stocks ended up across the board on Wednesday, starting the 2019 trading year on a positive foot, even as worries linger.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 18.78 points, or 0.08%, to 23346.24 while the S&P 500 gained 3.18 points, or 0.13%, to 2510.03, and the Nasdaq Composite added 30.66 points, or 0.46%, to 6665.94.
It’s not because the worries that torpedoed December have gone away, but at least 2018 has. Indeed, “the best thing we can say about the year gone by is that it’s over,” writes Credit Suisse’s Jonathan Golub . The losses were hard enough to stomach, but they came with quite a roller-coaster ride , with equities up 10% at their peak before plunging. And it’s not because we lacked fundamental reassurance, given gross domestic product and corporate earnings hit their best clip since 2011. “However, a litany of concerns around trade, the Fed, and decelerating growth have weighed heavily on stocks more recently,” Golub explains.
Trade. We were going to have to get to it sooner or later. Tariffs , along with slowing global growth and the government shutdown, formed a trifecta of worries that initially put investors off this morning, and it’s not hard to see why, with the looming deadline for the U.S. and China to come to an agreement. “At the very least, stocks likely can ill afford any escalation in tensions, and more likely will need some evidence of progress to push higher,” warns Amerprise’s David Joy .
Yet stocks were at least able to notch the first day of 2019 in positive territory, and despite all the negative headlines in the last month, it goes back to those fundamentals. Joy expects economic growth to remain “above trend” in 2019, and the “stamina needed by stocks to continue the fight has been restored to a certain extent by the significant improvement in valuations during the selloff...Stocks will continue to be tested, but don’t count them out just yet.”
While fears may have gotten the better of facts at the end of 2018, the silver lining is that now bulls have even more reason to jump back into the market. “Given the below-average valuations for the S&P 500 combined with expectations for mid- to high-single-digit earnings growth in 2019, this environment represents an opportunity to take advantage of the current disconnect between fundamentals and stock prices, from our perspective,” writes BMO Capital Markets’ Brian Belski .
Then there’s the fact that the U.S. economy remains strong. After the worst December since 1931, it might be easy to forget that we’re not actually in a recession—a statement that many believe will be just as true on December 31 as it is today. And when the S&P 500 suffers a bear market outside of a recession, the index tends to recover its losses in about half the time than it takes during a downturn. As Belski writes “It took only 95 days for the S&P 500 to fall 19.8%. Historically, the only two times that the index saw a greater than 19% drop in a shorter time frame was in 1998 and 1990- and the S&P 500 managed to climb to a new peak in just four and seven months, respectively.”
Markets can’t go up all the time, and might not tomorrow if Apple’s (AAPL) dreadful guidance , released after today’s close, weigh on the market. But the fact that investor appear willing to leave the worst of 2018 worries in the rearview mirror, shows that the inverse is also true: Pain too passes, especially when there are still reasons for optimism. The Hot Stock: Arconic Soars 10% on Takeover Talk
Arconic (ARNC) shot to the top of the S&P 500, on takeover reports.
Arconic rose $1.70, or 10.1%, to $18.56.
The metals maker got a boost from a Bloomberg report, which said that Apollo Global Management (APO) was in talks to buy the firm , in a deal that could close as soon as midmonth. Apollo closed up 1.1% to $24.82.
In the past year, Arconic is down 33.1%. The Biggest Loser: Hologic Sinks 6.5% Because Downgrades Hurt
Hologic (HOLX) sank to the bottom of the index following a downgrade.
Hologic lost $2.68, or 6.5%, to $38.42.
Morgan Stanley’s David Lewis downgraded the maker of diagnostics products and medical imaging systems to Underweight, citing “incremental risks and less compelling earnings power.” He prefers Baxter International (BAX), which he double-upgraded to Overweight from Underweight, as he sees top- and bottom-line acceleration into 2020. Baxter still closed down 0.8%.
Hologic is off 10.4% in the past year.
